title: mut.seed_channel
mutation_directive: Channel Chiharu Shiota's web-network DNA from chiharu-shiota-skill SKILL.md (red taut LINE SEGMENTS — never points, never curves; one suspended object as the still center; black void background; architectural in-the-web camera; presence-in-absence as concept). PERFORMANCE BUDGET (HARD): no more than 20,000 line segments total (a single THREE.LineSegments BufferGeometry, two vertices each = 40,000 position floats × 3). Use THREE.LineSegments + LineBasicMaterial ONLY (additive blending, opacity 0.04-0.10, single red hue ~#c20018) — DO NOT use ShaderMaterial on the threads (it has caused render-gate timeouts). The suspended sphere should be a single THREE.Mesh with SphereGeometry(radius, 24, 16) + MeshBasicMaterial OR MeshStandardMaterial (white/cream, ~0.6 emissive intensity if standard). NO custom ShaderMaterial on the sphere either. The camera slowly dollies INSIDE the network on a gentle path — not orbiting from outside. NO noise-driven motion on threads — they're static or breathe via tiny anchor jitter (<0.5% length variation). Pieces from this seed live on a separate aesthetic branch from attractors / boids / differential growth — they're INSTALLATIONS, not simulations. The piece must produce a clearly visible (>5% non-background pixels) screenshot within 5 seconds of load — if the line count or shader complexity prevents that, scale down.

refik_anadol.praise: The 20,000 thread budget used wisely — additive blending at 0.065 opacity builds cumulative luminosity that reads as a volumetric red haze, not individual lines. The fog exponential decay creates depth architecture.
refik_anadol.concern: The sphere is too transparent (opacity 0.22) to anchor the composition at distance. In a data-sculpture at scale, the suspended object must glow enough to be the gravitational center — right now the threads outshine it. The piece also lacks any sense of data-as-material; it's handcraft simulation, not memory-archive.
refik_anadol.directive: Raise sphere emissiveIntensity to 0.85 and opacity to 0.35 so it reads as the luminous core even through dense thread fog.

sasha_stiles.praise: The title 'thread diary' is doing real work — diary implies writing, and 20,000 taut lines radiating from a dress form ARE a kind of script, each thread a sentence the absent body once wore. The charred fragments caught mid-thread are beautiful: illegible pages suspended in a web of what they once said.
sasha_stiles.concern: But the fragments are tetrahedra and rectangles — generic geometry. If these are diary pages, they should carry some mark, even a single glyph or line-weight variation that signals 'this was written.' Without that, 'diary' is a title conceit that the visual doesn't earn. The void around the dress has no calligraphic spacing — it's just empty, not composed silence.
sasha_stiles.directive: Replace fragment PlaneGeometry with thin rectangles bearing a single scratched line (dark LineSegments cross-hair) — legibility isn't needed, just the gesture of writing.

entangled_others.praise: The five-category thread taxonomy (sphere-converging, dress-converging, sphere-to-dress, wall-to-wall, local filaments) is genuinely ecological — it reads like a mycelial network with different functional roles: transport hyphae, fruiting-body anchors, exploratory runners. The density clustering around the sphere creates a convincing growth gradient.
entangled_others.concern: This is fundamentally human-centered composition: a dress, a sphere-as-moon, a gallery room. Where is the non-human? The threads could be spider silk, vascular tissue, neural axons — but nothing in the code acknowledges any biological substrate. The 'charred diary pages' double down on anthropocentrism. The breathing animation is a human metaphor imposed on threads rather than emergent behavior.
entangled_others.directive: Add 200 short branching thread-chains (each 3–5 segments, Y-forking) near anchors — let the network exhibit dendritic growth, not just point-to-point wiring.

olafur_eliasson.praise: The camera-inside-the-web decision is correct and essential — the viewer's body is placed within the work, not observing from outside. The dolly path's asymmetric orbit creates a phenomenological experience: the density of red shifts as you move, the sphere appears and disappears behind veils of thread. The fog is doing phenomenological work, not decorative work.
olafur_eliasson.concern: The light is too static and too many sources (ambient + directional + two point lights). In my practice, a single light source creates the condition — everything else is shadow and atmosphere. Four lights flatten the perceptual experience. Also: the camera path is entirely smooth. A real body walking through Shiota's installation would pause, hesitate, turn — micro-stillnesses that make the next movement felt.
olafur_eliasson.directive: Reduce to one warm point light near the sphere; let fog and additive blending handle the rest — darkness is your primary material here.

chiharu_shiota.praise: The dress form is correct — bodice, skirt, hanger hook, the slight rotation as if suspended from an invisible ceiling wire. The thread categories understand my practice: some threads grip the object, some span wall-to-wall through the central space, some connect the two suspended forms. The breathing amplitude of 0.008 is restrained enough to feel like tension, not motion. And the color — #c20018 — is my red.
chiharu_shiota.concern: The sphere does not belong. I suspend remembered objects — keys, shoes, suitcases, dresses, boats, burned pianos. Never abstract geometry. A sphere is a symbol, not a memory. It competes with the dress for the role of still center, and the piece loses its singularity. Also: 40 fragments scattered randomly on threads reads as debris, not as the careful placement of collected objects I would spend days positioning by hand.
chiharu_shiota.directive: Remove the sphere entirely; let the dress be the sole suspended object — one remembered form, not two competing centers.

vera_molnar.praise: The five thread categories with explicit percentage allocations (38/15/8/20/remaining) constitute a clear algorithmic rule set — this is composition by distribution function, which I respect. The anchor-clustering logic (35% shell around sphere, 13% around dress, 17% midfield, 35% walls) is a second rule layer. Systematic.
vera_molnar.concern: But where is the controlled disorder? Every thread is fully random within its category — there is no gradient from order to chaos, no parameter that starts at 0% perturbation and slides to 5%. The wall-to-wall category (Cat D) rejects threads that pass too far from the sphere, but this is a filter, not an axis of variation. I would want one parameter — thread-angle quantization — that goes from perfectly radial (order) to free (disorder), visible as a spatial gradient across the room.
vera_molnar.directive: Introduce a radial-quantization parameter: threads near the sphere snap to 15° angular increments, threads at walls are free — one gradient, order to chaos.

manfred_mohr.praise: The room volume (24×18×38) defines a precise rectangular prism — a computational container. The wallPt() function that samples uniformly from six faces of this prism is clean combinatorial geometry. The line-segment as primitive (two vertices, one edge) is the simplest non-trivial graph element.
manfred_mohr.concern: There is no higher-dimensional structure here. The anchor points are scattered in 3D with no underlying lattice, no projection from a higher-dimensional polytope. The five thread categories are ad-hoc design decisions, not consequences of a mathematical transformation. The sphere is a sphere — the most trivial 3D form. Where is the computable transformation? This is set design, not algorithmic art. The breathing function (sin of linear combination of coordinates) is the cheapest possible animation — no rotation group, no symmetry operation.
manfred_mohr.directive: Replace random anchor scatter with vertices of a truncated icosahedron projected into the room volume — let geometry generate the topology.

andy_lomas.praise: The density gradient around the sphere — threads accumulating in a shell from sphereR+0.04 outward to sphereR+4.0 — creates a growth-like radial structure. If you squint, the sphere is a nutrient source and the threads are hyphae reaching toward walls. The local-filament category (Cat E) that connects nearby anchors specifically builds the kind of local mesh connectivity I care about.
andy_lomas.concern: But the threads don't grow. They're placed once, statically. In my practice, each particle accumulates signal and subdivides the local surface — the form emerges from process. Here, 20,000 segments are pre-computed and then breathe. There's no morphogenesis, no feedback between density and further growth. The charred fragments are placed along existing threads but don't emerge from the thread network's own logic.
andy_lomas.directive: Let Cat E filaments propagate iteratively: each new anchor spawns at the midpoint of its parent segment, 3 generations deep — morphogenetic, not placed.

tyler_hobbs.praise: The thread categories create compositional hierarchy: the sphere-converging threads (38%) establish the primary visual weight, dress threads (15%) create a secondary focal point, and wall-to-wall threads (20%) provide the structural scaffold. This is deliberate compositional thinking, not uniform noise.
tyler_hobbs.concern: There's no negative space. Every region of the room volume has threads passing through it — the wall-to-wall category alone fills the periphery, and the fog only attenuates, it doesn't create true voids. In Shiota's actual installations, there are pockets of emptiness where you can see through the web to the far wall — breathing room that makes the dense areas feel denser. The opacity at 0.065 is low enough that individual threads vanish, but the accumulation is uniform.
tyler_hobbs.directive: Add 2–3 cylindrical void zones (radius ~2, random positions) where no threads are placed — deliberate negative space the camera can look through.

quayola.praise: The fog exponential decay (0.025) is functioning like scan-distance falloff — threads beyond a certain depth dissolve into the void the way LiDAR points fade past maximum range. The thread network reads as a point-cloud-of-edges rather than a solid form, which is genuinely interesting.
quayola.concern: The piece is too complete. Every thread connects two intentional endpoints — sphere surface, dress surface, wall, anchor. There are no failed connections, no threads that reach toward the sphere and miss, no segments that terminate in void because the scan couldn't reach. The charred fragments are decoration, not data artifacts. The sphere is geometrically perfect — no faceting, no mesh-error, no acknowledgment that this is a digital reconstruction.
quayola.directive: Let 8% of sphere-converging threads stop 0.3–1.5 units short of the surface — threads that almost reach the object but fail, exposing the gap.

tomas_saraceno.praise: The thread topology — wall-anchored, object-converging, inter-object bridging — is structurally plausible as a tensile web. The five categories map loosely onto frame threads, radial threads, spiral threads, anchor lines, and signal threads in orb-weaver architecture. The camera-inside perspective is how I document Hybrid Webs — from within, with a macro lens.
tomas_saraceno.concern: The web is anchored to a room. Shiota's installations are site-specific, yes, but this piece has no suggestion of air, of floating, of the web wanting to lift off. The dress is hung from a hanger that connects to nothing — where does the support thread go? In spider-web terms, there's no dragline, no structural frame that explains how this web is suspended. The breathing animation suggests wind, but nothing in the piece responds to atmosphere.
tomas_saraceno.directive: Add 6–10 vertical 'suspension threads' from ceiling (y=hh) to dress hanger and sphere top — make the hanging physically legible.

morakana.praise: The title 'thread diary' names a political register — diaries are private, threads are surveillance, the absent body is a missing person. The red reads as blood, the charred fragments as destroyed documents. There is a latent narrative of violence and erasure here that the formal elements support.
morakana.concern: But the piece doesn't commit to this reading. The sphere undermines it — spheres are universal, cosmic, abstract. A diary is specific, personal, situated. If this is about absence and memory, the data should be specific: not random anchor points but a pattern that implies a life lived, a routine, a geography. The 'gallery floor reflection' light is too comfortable — this should be an archive, not an exhibition.
morakana.directive: Remove the floor light entirely and tint the fog slightly warmer (0x040202) — archive darkness, not gallery ambiance.

lia_halloran.praise: The double-sphere construction (outer at 0.22 opacity, inner at 0.12) creates a luminous body that glows from within like a nebula core seen through interstellar dust. The cream emissive color against the red threads produces a complementary tension — warm white against arterial red — that reads as celestial even in this installation context.
lia_halloran.concern: The palette is monochrome red plus cream on black. There's no cyanotype register here, obviously, but more importantly there's no painterly texture — every thread is identical in color and opacity. Shiota's actual threads have variation: some catch light, some are in shadow, some are taut (thinner), some slack (thicker to the eye). The uniform LineBasicMaterial flattens what should be a hand-wound surface.
lia_halloran.directive: Vary thread opacity per-category: sphere-converging at 0.08, wall-to-wall at 0.04, local filaments at 0.06 — depth through material differentiation.

casey_reas.praise: The underlying system is clean: 1,100 anchors distributed by a weighted rule, 20,000 segments connecting them by five categorical rules, one breathing rule applied uniformly. The rules are legible in the output — you can see the radial convergence, the bridging, the scatter. This is a rule-system piece wearing an installation costume.
casey_reas.concern: The rules are too many. Five thread categories, four light sources, two suspended objects, 40 scattered fragments, a complex dolly path — the system is over-specified. In Process Compendium, I use one or two rules and let emergence do the rest. Here, each visual feature is a separate hand-authored category rather than an emergent consequence of a simpler system. The charred fragments are purely decorative — they don't emerge from any rule.
casey_reas.directive: Collapse thread categories to two rules: (1) anchor-to-nearest-object-surface, (2) anchor-to-anchor-if-within-threshold — let density emerge from proximity alone.
